model.source_system: Sliding puzzle / n-puzzle family (15 puzzle; Klotski is the sliding-block cognate; rules public), transcribed as the 2x3 deterministic variant: 5 numbered tiles + 1 open position, 4 slide directions, no randomness collected, no score
model.source_citation: Wikipedia "15 puzzle" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15_puzzle): lead ("Tiles in the same row or column of the open position can be moved by sliding them horizontally or vertically, respectively."; "The goal of the puzzle is to place the tiles in numerical order (from left to right, top to bottom)."; "the 8 puzzle, which has 8 tiles in a 3x3 frame"), Solvability section ("Johnson & Story (1879) used a parity argument to show that half of the starting positions for the n puzzle are impossible to resolve"; "on boards of size m x n, where m and n are both larger than or equal to 2, all even permutations are solvable"); Wikipedia "Sliding puzzle" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sliding_puzzle): lead ("a combination puzzle that challenges a player to slide (frequently flat) pieces along certain routes (usually on a board) to establish a certain end-configuration"; "a sliding block puzzle prohibits lifting any pieces off the board"), with Klotski listed among the examples of sliding puzzles. Per-rule citations in meta.rules_with_citations; per-edge generating rules in meta.edge_rule_tags.
